subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after source-level OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The remaining decision controls whether private scheduled or channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repository policy treats auth/provider routing and fallback behavior as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep this open until live `sessions_spawn` proof shows OAuth inheritance works and define either fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split fallback visibility after auth proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation part after live proof and track user-visible fallback behavior in a narrower issue.

options.title: Accept log-only fallback
options.body: Treat the current structured fallback logs as sufficient after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open until live `sessions_spawn` proof shows OAuth inheritance works and define either fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing owner from the auth-profile, OpenAI identity, Codex bridge, and subagent/session history.
